pass_a_gloss: Clearly it is written in the Acts of the Apostles that the apostles first entered the synagogue of the Jews, proclaiming to them as kin through Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob the things written about the coming of Jesus Christ; but when those things spoken were not received by them, it was necessary to have other hearers of the things spoken, so after making their defense they left them; for it is written that 'It was necessary that the word of God be spoken to you first; but since you judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles.' This is clearly said in the Acts of the Apostles with power in many places and also spoken by the prophets; for indeed beforehand the Holy Spirit speaks through the holy prophets to those from that people, but if ever after speaking much it was not heard, the Spirit prophesies the word being proclaimed to the Gentiles. And this also came to pass at the beginning of today's reading, because before this it was said to those from Israel: 'If even you call me father, and do not turn away from me; yet as a woman acts treacherously against her companion, so the house of Israel has acted treacherously against me,' says the Lord. And when these things had been spoken beforehand concerning Israel and the sons of Israel heard them, saying: 'They have dealt falsely in their ways and have forgotten their holy God,' then next the Holy Spirit transfers the word to us from the nations and says: 'Return, O backsliding children, and I will heal your wounds.' For we are those filled with wounds; each one could say, even if now cleansed and healed from wounds: 'We too were once foolish, foolish, wandering, serving lusts and pleasures many and various, in malice and envy hateful, hating one another.' But when the kindness and love of our Savior God appeared, through the washing of regeneration he poured out his mercy upon us (and even that apostolic statement once mentioned I will try to demonstrate more clearly. For he did not say: 'We were once foolish, disobedient'; but Paul, the apostle, from Israel, the one 'who became blameless according to righteousness in the law,' says: 'We too were once (those from Israel) disobedient, foolish'; but not only were those from the Gentiles foolish, nor only those from the nations disobedient, nor only those sinners, but we also, who were taught the law, were such before the coming of Christ. Therefore it is said after the things spoken to Israel toward us from the nations: 'Return, O backsliding children, and I will heal your wounds.'

variants.note: Μνῶν in lock treated as ἐθνῶν ('nations'), not Moab; Pass A corrected.
